category_title: Student with EBD who yells, throws objects, and wanders during instruction
minimal_context: Malcolm is assigned an independent math worksheet to complete by himself in the pull-out special education classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is your independent math worksheet. I need you to work on this by yourself for the next ten minutes while I sit at my desk.

STUDENT: This is too hard! I'm not doing this stupid math.

TUTOR: Just try to answer the questions on your own.

STUDENT: (Stands up and starts wandering around the classroom) I said I'm not doing it! You're ugly anyway!

TUTOR: Please go back to your desk and keep trying.

STUDENT: (Yells loudly, throws the pencil across the room, and drops to roll on the floor) No! I'm not doing it!

options.A: Set a timer on a fixed 1-minute interval schedule and provide specific performance feedback based on the student's behavior (e.g., 'great job working').
options.B: Agree with the student that he is having a rough time completing the independent math worksheet during the session.
options.C: Provide increased opportunities for the student to exercise control (e.g., select worksheets, choose materials, determine the order of math problems).
options.D: Prompt the student to use a stress ball if he begins throwing objects during the independent math worksheet.
